quotes.verbatim: A '''King Crimson''' is a [[T-Spin Triple]] layered on top of a [[Super T-Spin Double]] which can be performed when the playfield has a single block in the bottom left or bottom right corner.
It can also be used as a continuation of the [[TKI_3_Opening|TKI 3]] opener.
After the first or second T-Spin from a [[TKI_3_Opening|TKI 3]] setup, a King Crimson bonus is possible.
This is usually not suggested due to its high height and the 3 T pieces necessary to complete the setup.

variants.window_note: in basic.spin's frame, row 0 the top: the AGREEMENT BOX of this page's four drawings of the shape and two drawings on two other harddrop pages, each selected by that page's own King Crimson label. Column 6 is the well's wall (filled top to bottom), column 7 the well (the overhang over it in row 0, empty from row 1 down), column 8 the TST slot's far side and the STSD's nub column, column 9 the wall column on the open side. Rows 2-4 are the rows the TST clears (entailed by the clear at a full TST, NaiveClauseForced); above them the overhang (row 0) and the row under it (row 1, open on the far side); under them the STSD slot (rows 5-7: its nub row walled by the far column's S, its bottom cell under the T, the cell beside it open). Left of column 6, and above row 0, is outside: the drawings disagree there (column 5 of row 0) or one of them ends (the basic setup's top row). Occupancy only, never colour; garbage is filled.

followup.note: the STSD: a second T stood up into the lower slot, nub toward the open side, credited as a full T-spin Double (the page: 「a [[T-Spin Triple]] layered on top of a [[Super T-Spin Double]]」). Its cells are all under the TST's three cleared rows, so the clear does not move or split them; the matcher carries the slot to the next T all the same.

cross_source.note: the window, by the gate's predicate (technique_transcription.window_fires), over every U-slot board of every committed *-routes.json, with the U cells as the T: it fires on none (no route page draws a King Crimson). The independent drawers are two other harddrop pages (`pages`), whose King Crimson drawings are the window's external `agreement` drawings: rule (g) fires the window on each, once, at its slot, in its recorded hand.
